newsitem.title: USA: In Home Health to reduce Medicare reliance.
newsitem.headline: In Home Health to reduce Medicare reliance.

text.p: In Home Health Inc, which posted a loss for the fourth quarter and fiscal year ended September 30 on lower revenue, said its fiscal 1997 focus to improving profitability will involve less reliance on Medicare.

To improve profitability and boost revenue in fiscal 1997, chief executive officer Mark Gildea said the company will take certain steps. "This will include reducing our dependence on Medicare, resolving Medicare disputes and obtaining accreditation from the Joint Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Organizations," he said in a statement.
Gildea also said the home health nursing services company will continue to develop specialized products and work to lower its costs.
Earlier, In Home Health reported a fourth-quarter loss of $0.12 per share compared with a year-ago profit of $0.03. Revenues fell to $30.5 million from $32.7 million.
The 1996 quarter included charges of $1.6 million from settlements with the company's former officers and charges of $700,000 for relocations and other severance agreements.
